content: Superficial anatomy, also referred to as surface anatomy or visual anatomy, is a branch of anatomical science that focuses on the external features of the body that can be observed without dissection. In humans, this includes the shape, proportions, and surface landmarks of the body, which correspond to deeper structures that are not visible externally. These features can be studied both in a static position and during movement. Superficial anatomy also encompasses theories and systems related to body proportions, which have historically influenced artistic representations of the human form. Additionally, certain pseudosciences, such as physiognomy, phrenology, and palmistry, have drawn upon superficial anatomy, though their relationship to it is analogous to the relationship between astrology and astronomy—one-sided and not scientifically validated. Below is a detailed list of superficial anatomical features, organized from cranial (head) to caudal (tail) regions. Homologous structures are grouped together, and subcomponents are nested. Alternative names or specific classifications are noted where applicable. 1. Tentacle: Found in Cephalopoda. 2. Head: Antler Crest Hood Horn Mane Eyes Ears Snout: Includes the nose and trunk. Nostrils Whiskers Beak: Found only in Aves. Mouth: Lips: Not present in Aves. Philtrum Jaw: Not present in Aves. Gums: Not present in Aves. Teeth: Not present in Aves. Tusk Tongue 3. Throat: Adam’s apple Vocal sac: Found in Ranidae (frogs). 4. Spine: Extends dorsally. 5. Tail 6. Arm: Found in Mammalia and Amphibia; fin in fish; wing in Aves. Elbow Wrist Hand: Fingers: Includes the thumb in primates. Hoof, claw, nails Webbing 7. Chest (approximately the thorax): Gills Breast: Found in Mammalia. 8. Abdomen (approximately the stomach): Pouch: Found in Marsupialia. Genitals: In females: Vulva In males: Penis Scrotum 9. Leg: Thigh Knee Kneecap Shin Calf Ankle Foot: Toes Hoof 10. Skin: Feathers: Found in Aves. Scales: Found in Reptilia. Hair: Found in Mammalia. Shell This list provides a comprehensive breakdown of visible anatomical features across various species, highlighting their structural and functional diversity.
